messages:
maya: Heads-up — I ran a quick tail-latency sweep on console queries and RBAC checks are spiking p99 for some dashboard tiles (~120ms -> 450ms) after the recent rule layering change.
kevin: ugh. is that the new hierarchical policy evaluation we rolled out?
anita: yes, the new evaluator fetches tenant policies + feature flags per-request. we probably forgot to cache the merged policy.
maya: exact. repro from local: single tile query -> query-layer calls authz svc sync, code looks like:```python
policy = authz.fetch(tenant, resource)
if not policy.allow(query):
    raise Forbidden
# then run heavy projection```
phil: two quick options: 1) move a subset of checks (read-only view-level allow/deny) into a pre-computed prefix so the hot path doesn't call authz; or 2) make authz async + optimistic allow with fallback. both have tradeoffs.
kevin: pref 1 for safety. precompute means storing {view_id: allowed_tenants} or a short ACL fingerprint we can check in-mem. downside is invalidation complexity on policy updates.
anita: agreed, invalidation is the kicker. current change propagation is eventual (~5s). for SLAs we might need near-real-time.
maya: idea: hybrid — precompute a lightweight bloom-filter style fingerprint per-tenant for fast deny/hit checks; still do a background strong check for edge cases. fingerprint can be recomputed on policy change stream.
phil: +1 on fingerprint. cheap in-memory check avoids RPC. we should measure false-positive rate and ensure false positives map to performing the heavy sync check (so correctness preserved).
kevin: implementation notes: store fingerprint in the tile cache entry metadata; query execution path should check fingerprint first, then short-circuit to run tile query. invalidation hook on policy stream should mark affected tiles stale.
anita: would need a utility to compute delta updates on policy change so we don't rebuild all fingerprints. we already have a policy-change kafka topic — can consume and emit affected view_ids.
maya: perf plan: benchmark p50/p95/p99 before/after with mixed tenant load and 10k concurrent tiles. target p99 < 200ms.
phil: ops concerns: what if authz-bot or service is down? fingerprint allows degraded read-only behavior for a short window (ttl). we should document fallback: if fingerprint missing -> pessimistic check (sync RPC) for safety.
kevin: sounds good. can someone volunteer to prototype the fingerprint encoder + integration test? small spike, 2-3 days.
anita: I can take the spike. will push a draft PR and include a simple CLI to compute fingerprints from policy dumps.
maya: awesome — please include perf harness and a togglable feature flag so we can rollout canary (10% of traffic) then ramp.
authz-bot: deploy plan template created: https://go/repo/infra/authz-fingerprint-deploy (uses canary, metrics: authz_rpc_count, tile_p99_ms, false_positive_rate).
phil: add an alert if false_positive_rate > 0.5% for 10m during canary.
kevin: ok next steps: anita -> spike + PR, maya -> perf harness + benchmark baselines, phil -> alerting runbook. sync Friday 11am. :calendar:
maya: thanks — noted.
